newsitem.title: JAPAN: NIPPON LIFE TO ACCEPT REQUEST TO BUY NCB SHARES.
newsitem.headline: NIPPON LIFE TO ACCEPT REQUEST TO BUY NCB SHARES.

text.p: Nippon Life Insurance Co said on Monday that it would accept a request from Nippon Credit Bank Ltd to help the troubled long-term credit bank increase its capital.
Industry sources said that Nippon Life's decision to buy NCB shares would help convince other financial institutions to accept NCB's plan to boost its capital by 290.7 billion yen.
A Nippon Life spokesman said NCB would first repay 50 billion yen in perpetual subordinated loans provided by Nippon Life to NCB.
Nippon Life would then use half of that money to buy ordinary NCB shares and use the other 25 billion yen to make new term-subordinated loans to NCB.
Nippon Life has already provided term-subordinated loans worth 13 billion yen to NCB, the spokesman said.
Under the plan, the bank will repay 3.25 billion yen of those loans, which the insurer will also use to buy NCB's preferred stock, he said.

In April, NCB announced a plan to boost its capital by 290.7 billion yen, relying on a Bank of Japan investment of 80 billion yen through a financial system stabilisation fund, as well as a total investment of 70 billion yen by big commercial and long-term credit banks.
Major life and nonlife insurance firms have also been requested to convert subordinated loans worth 140.7 billion yen into NCB shares.

Nippon Life has been reluctant to convert its subordinated loans into NCB shares while many big Japanese banks have said that they would purchase new NCB shares on condition that other financial institutions also agree to NCB's request, the sources said.
